title: Clone Graph
algorithm: DFS / BFS with Node Hash Map
oneLinerQuestion: Create a deep copy of a connected, undirected graph.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Clone Graph problem asks for a deep copy of a connected undirected graph where each node contains an integer value and a list of its neighbors. A deep copy requires that every node and edge be recreated as a brand new instance in memory without reusing original node references. Because undirected graphs often contain cycles, a naive traversal will get trapped in an infinite recursive loop. To solve this, we use Depth-First Search (DFS) combined with a Hash Map that maps each original node to its newly created clone, serving both as a memoized visited tracker and as an address book for wiring cloned adjacency lists.

- Step 1: Base Case & Setup — If `node === null`, the graph is empty, so we immediately return `null`. We initialize a hash map `visited = new Map()` where keys are references to original nodes and values are references to their cloned counterparts.

- Step 2: Recursive DFS Helper Definition — We define a helper function `dfs(currNode)` that handles the duplication of `currNode` and recursively explores and links all its adjacent vertices.

- Step 3: Visited Node Lookup (Cycle Prevention) — At the start of `dfs(currNode)`, we check `if (visited.has(currNode))`. If the node has already been cloned, we return its mapped clone instance (`visited.get(currNode)`), which short-circuits cycles and stops infinite recursion.

- Step 4: Clone Instantiation & Map Registration — If `currNode` has not been cloned yet, we instantiate a new node with the identical value: `const clone = new Node(currNode.val)`. We immediately register it in the lookup table: `visited.set(currNode, clone)`. This registration must happen before inspecting neighbors to handle cyclical cross-edges correctly.

- Step 5: Neighbor Traversal & Edge Stitching — We iterate over each neighbor in `currNode.neighbors`: for each neighbor, we recursively invoke `dfs(neighbor)` and append the returned cloned reference into `clone.neighbors.push(...)`.

- Step 6: Termination & Root Clone Return — Once all neighbor branches resolve and their corresponding edges are mirrored, `dfs(currNode)` returns `clone`. Initiating `dfs(node)` from the input root node produces a fully copied, isolated replica of the entire graph component.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(V + E) where V is the number of vertices (nodes) and E is the number of edges, as DFS traverses each node and evaluates each edge exactly once. Space Complexity: O(V) auxiliary space to store the original-to-clone mapping in the hash map and manage the DFS recursion stack.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION cloneGraph(node):
    IF node IS NULL THEN RETURN NULL
    visited = EMPTY_HASH_MAP()
    FUNCTION dfs(n):
        IF n IN visited THEN RETURN visited[n]
        copy = NEW Node(n.val)
        visited[n] = copy
        FOR neighbor IN n.neighbors DO:
            APPEND dfs(neighbor) TO copy.neighbors
        END FOR
        RETURN copy
    END FUNCTION
    RETURN dfs(node)
END FUNCTION
